title: A lane can fix its own branch: the red-run check stops asking for a force push, and auto mode lets a lease push to a lane's own branch
why: Owner answer on page item 257 (Nov 5 07:44 CST): "shouldn't it be c and d". 9 lease-push refusals and 8 replacement PRs, Nov 2 to 4; 5 of 9 came from the red-run check's remedy naming a bare --force-with-lease.
note: Nov 5 08:33 CST (lane): part d is draft PR #1255 (the red-run check's remedy names no force push), handed to batch runner 8. Part c is the owner's paste into settings.json, page item 262; it also covers 239 a. Nov 5 07:52 CST (coordinator): the lane does d only; the classifier refused the brief for c (Self-Modification), so c is an owner paste into settings.json (text given in chat 07:48 CST), covering 257 c and 239 a. Lane session_013NEJL37QndQaqk1XZCmK4x, started Nov 5 07:47 CST (coordinator). Page item 257. Build d first: lint/check_red_run.py's remedy points at a route with no force push (or the trailer is checked before the first push), so its remedy and the force-push guard's stop disagreeing. Then c: an autoMode.allow prose entry in decision auto-mode-owner-acts, like Archived Branch Delete: a lease push to a branch this session pushed earlier, never default, archive/, roadmap or merge-lock; the classifier still judges. c is a permission change only the owner can make; his page answer is the word. Try c on a real lane fix and record whether the classifier lets it through. Owner session for the question: lane restore-roadmap-fork-test.
